name: GNOME / Adwaita
era: Contemporary design system · authored web adaptation
idea: A focused window gathers a few main actions in its header and related content in a quiet list.
origin: Adwaita and libadwaita shape GNOME applications. GNOME guidelines combine a focused task with adaptable windows. Header bars combine a window title and contextual actions. This demo is an authored HTML adaptation.
tip: Choose one clear main task and keep only its frequent actions in the header. Then check narrow windows.

finder.signature: Centered window title, few primary actions and a boxed list.

strengths: A focused window gathers a few main actions in its header and related content in a quiet list.
A documented system supports consistent component decisions.
risks: A minimal header must not make important actions undiscoverable.
These colors, sizes and radii describe this demo, not a full vendor token specification.
The web adaptation does not reproduce native window management, assistive technology integration or device input.
a11y: Test visible keyboard focus, screen-reader names, 200% text resizing and contrast in every state. Use system colors for native implementations and retain text labels for status. These editorial scores are not an accessibility certification.
longevity: Stable hierarchy and task structure outlast individual theme generations. Check current platform components when implementing.
verdict: A focused window gathers a few main actions in its header and related content in a quiet list. Choose one clear main task and keep only its frequent actions in the header. Then check narrow windows.

platforms.web: Authored HTML/CSS comparison; use semantic controls in a product.
platforms.mobile: The list becomes a single boxed group. The title stays compact and actions retain labels. This demonstrates adaptiveness, not a native GNOME phone interface.
platforms.desktop: The broad reference shows the system’s task hierarchy. Actual native applications also need platform navigation and input conventions.
